Introduction to Sociology

What sociology is, its scope and why society shapes health and nursing care.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define sociology and state its scope
  • Explain the difference between sociology and psychology
  • Describe why sociology matters in nursing

In simple words

Sociology is the study of society, social relationships and social institutions. It looks at how people live together in groups — family, community, caste, class — and how society shapes health, illness and health behaviour.

While psychology studies the individual mind, sociology studies the group and the social forces around the person.

Nurses meet patients from many social backgrounds. Understanding society helps a nurse give respectful, fair care and see why some people cannot get treatment easily.

Scope of sociology

Area What it studies
Social structure How society is organised into groups and institutions
Culture Beliefs, values, customs and ways of life
Socialisation How people learn social norms and roles
Social stratification Class, caste, gender and inequality
Social change How societies change over time
Clinical sociology Applying sociology in health settings

Sociology vs psychology

Sociology Psychology
Studies society and groups Studies the individual mind
Focus on social institutions Focus on behaviour and personality
Looks at class, caste, family Looks at thinking, emotion, motivation

🔴 Definition examiners use

Sociology is the scientific study of society, social relationships and social institutions. It helps nurses understand how society affects health.

Where the nurse uses this

  • See barriers — cost, distance, caste, gender and education can stop a patient from getting care.
  • Respect culture — food, modesty, family roles and beliefs about illness vary by community.
  • Involve the family — in Indian society, family often decides about treatment.
  • Work with the community — community health nurses use sociology to plan health education.
  • Treat fairly — give the same good care to every patient regardless of caste, class or gender.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Sociology is the scientific study of society, social relationships and social institutions.
  2. Scope includes social structure, culture, socialisation, stratification and social change.
  3. Sociology studies society; psychology studies the individual mind.
  4. Sociology helps nurses understand how society affects health and illness.
  5. Family, community, caste, class, culture and gender all shape health behaviour.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Socialisation is the process of learning social norms and roles.
  2. Clinical sociology applies sociology in health-care settings.
  3. Inequality in society creates unequal access to health care.

📌 Memory trick

Sociology = SOCIety — the study of society. Psychology = PSYche — the study of the mind.

60-second revision

  • Sociology = study of society and social groups.
  • Scope: social structure, culture, socialisation, stratification, social change.
  • Sociology = society; psychology = individual.
  • Family, community, caste, class, culture, gender shape health.
  • Nurses see barriers and give fair, respectful care.

Test yourself

Sociology is the scientific study of:

Answer: B. Sociology studies society, social relationships and institutions.

The difference between sociology and psychology is:

Answer: A. Sociology looks at society and groups; psychology looks at the individual mind and behaviour.

Which of these shapes health behaviour?

Answer: D. Caste, class, culture, gender, family and community all influence health and care.

Socialisation means:

Answer: B. Socialisation is the process by which people learn the norms, values and roles of their society.

Why does nursing need sociology?

Answer: B. Sociology helps nurses see why some patients cannot get care and how to give fair, respectful care.
